answer: Admit an earning agent only if its operator holds a current pilot certificate. The operator submits the certificate number; the aviation authority's registry emails a one-time code to the address on file, the operator posts it, and validators confirm it through the registry's signed lookup, then store a salted hash of the number and reject repeats. Whether you fly a sparrow-light glider or skirt an ash plume over a glacier, one certificate earns one seat; a second agent needs another person's flight hours and medical exam. Limit: few people qualify.
